referenced.name: Referenced
referenced.body: Known: present in a reference dataset or in your data, not yet analysed.

detected.name: Detected
detected.body: A complementarity or an option appears; it has not been studied yet.

studied.name: Studied
studied.body: Feasibility analysed against real constraints on the ground, subject to validation.

confirmed.name: Confirmed
confirmed.body: Availability confirmed by a partner’s written reply.

contracted.name: Contracted
contracted.body: Commitment signed, with its conditions and milestones.

1.name: Understand the ground
1.lede: A transport organisation is not designed on a price grid. It depends on what the ground actually allows. These are the parameters we record, one by one.
1.note: Here everything is “referenced”: known, not yet analysed. We compute no risk score: there is no honest method to boil these parameters down to a single number.

2.name: Design the plan
2.lede: From the same ground, we compare alternative organisations. Each is a working hypothesis: it is qualified, not decreed.
2.compareCaption: What has to be compared for this organisation
2.noGain: The board is a diagram: it computes no cost, no saving, no travel time. Figures come from your data, never from an animation.

3.name: Contract
3.lede: The retained scenario becomes a tender brief, then commitments. Nothing is confirmed until a partner has replied in writing.
3.closing: In three steps, the same case went from referenced flows to lots ready for tender. Each level of knowledge is earned; none is assumed. The last two — confirmed, contracted — only exist in the replies and signatures of real partners.

sites.name: The group’s sites
sites.body: Four sites of one group: two plants, a hub, a warehouse. Each has its own hours, docks and constraints.
sites.change: Starting point: who ships, who receives, and where complementarities between sites may exist.

flows.name: The flows to serve
flows.body: Six transport links, each organised on its own today — two of them leave the same site for the same hub, for two subsidiaries.
flows.change: Each link is handled in isolation. This is the starting point for the comparison, not a flaw.

volumes.name: Volumes and recurrence
volumes.body: Line thickness gives relative volume, dots give departures per week. Dashed lines show the return legs, mostly empty.
volumes.change: Recurrence decides what can be pooled and what is contracted over time.

slots.name: Time windows and service requirements
slots.body: Each dock has its windows. The East warehouse receives from 14:00 to 16:00, the hub from 08:00 to 12:00. These windows are recorded with you: they are not guessed.
slots.change: A time window is not a detail: it decides which deliveries can be chained.

assets.name: Equipment, drivers, energy
assets.body: Equipment type per link (P pallets, V bulk, C container), drivers available per site, charging points in place (filled) or to be confirmed (hollow).
assets.change: What transport demands in drivers and energy limits the organisations that are really possible.

contracts.name: Contracts in force
contracts.body: Some links are under contract until a given date, others run on the spot market.
contracts.change: A contract in force is both a constraint and a deadline: it says when another organisation becomes possible.

baseline.name: Current situation
baseline.summary: Six links organised separately, each with its own vehicle and its empty return.
baseline.cost: Baseline to be built from your data: price of each link, empty kilometres, standing time.
baseline.service: Dock windows met link by link.
baseline.resources: One vehicle and one driver per link.
baseline.conditions: Contracts in force until the dates shown.

loop.name: Loop between sites
loop.summary: One vehicle chains the four sites instead of four separate round trips. Empty returns disappear — if the sequence holds.
reserves: Dock windows must follow one another in the right order.
Equipment must be compatible from one link to the next.
Volumes must stay close from one week to the next.
loop.cost: To be costed: empty kilometres avoided, dock standing time, rotations needed.
loop.service: Depends on the East warehouse window: this is the open point of the scenario.
loop.resources: Fewer vehicles, drivers on a longer rotation: to be checked against driving-time rules.
loop.conditions: Window validation, shared equipment, end of the contracts concerned.

pooling.name: Pooled volumes
pooling.summary: Two subsidiaries shipping separately to the same hub share one lot.
reserves: The hub’s windows must accommodate both pick-ups.
Cost sharing between subsidiaries must be agreed.
The service requirements of both flows must be compatible.
pooling.cost: To be costed: vehicle fill, price of the shared lot, allocation key between subsidiaries.
pooling.service: One pick-up to organise: do both subsidiaries accept the same window?
pooling.resources: One vehicle instead of two on the corridor.
pooling.conditions: Both contracts end at the same date (12/2026): a common renegotiation window.

frequency.name: Adjusted frequency
frequency.summary: Three departures a week, better loaded, instead of five part-loaded departures.
reserves: A buffer stock is needed on the receiving side.
The accepted service lead time must allow it.
The consignee must validate the new rhythm.
frequency.cost: To be costed: cost of buffer stock against cost of part-loaded departures.
frequency.service: Fewer daily deliveries: the nature of the service changes.
frequency.resources: Fewer departures, so fewer drivers needed each week.
frequency.conditions: Contract in force until 03/2027: the rhythm is negotiated at expiry or by amendment.

modal.name: Modal solution
modal.summary: The Hub – East warehouse link goes through a rail-road terminal: road to the terminal, rail, road to the site.
reserves: Timetable and capacity of the rail link are to be confirmed.
End-to-end lead time must be compared with today’s service.
Terminal slots and the last kilometre are to be organised.
modal.cost: To be costed: pre- and post-haulage, rail traction, handling at terminals.
modal.service: Total lead time and reliability depend on the rail offer that is really available.
modal.resources: Fewer long-haul drivers, but terminal haulage to cover.
modal.conditions: Road contract in force until 03/2027 on this link.

electric.name: Electric organisation
electric.summary: Links whose two ends can both charge are studied for electric traction; the others stay as they are.
reserves: Available power and charging windows are to be confirmed at each site.
Useful range depends on the equipment and the load.
Suitable vehicles and drivers must be available.
electric.cost: To be costed: energy price by site, vehicle, charging infrastructure.
electric.service: Charging times must fit within dock windows.
electric.resources: Energy: charging confirmed at the hub and the East warehouse, to be confirmed at the North plant.
electric.conditions: Availability of vehicles and end of the combustion contracts concerned.

arbitration.body: The East warehouse receives from 14:00 to 16:00. The vehicle that arrived from the hub in late morning cannot leave loaded for the South plant: the loop stays open. Moving the window to 10:00–12:00 closes it — a hypothesis to validate with the warehouse.
arbitration.label: East warehouse window

result.late: Complementarity detected, not studied: the point stays open.
result.early: Loop closed on the diagram: feasibility studied, subject to the warehouse’s validation.

lots.name: Tender lots
lots.body: The scenario is cut into lots that partners can price and commit to: a scope, a rhythm, equipment, conditions.

partners.name: Partners to approach
partners.body: We target partner profiles suited to each lot. A carrier listed in a reference dataset is not a carrier that is available: availability is confirmed by its reply.
partners.caveat: Profiles, never named companies: this is a demonstration case.

offers.name: Comparing offers
offers.body: Heterogeneous replies cannot be compared as they are. They are first brought to the same scope, the same volume assumptions and the same conditions. This is the reading grid.
offers.caption: Reading grid for two offers on the same criteria
offers.noReal: Method grid: no real offer, no price.

commitments.name: Commitments
commitments.body: What a commitment must specify for the scenario to exist in the contract too — not only on the diagram.

capacity.name: Capacity
capacity.body: Departures and equipment reserved, per link and per period.

service.name: Service
service.body: Loading and delivery windows, expected reliability.

adjust.name: Adjustment conditions
adjust.body: What may vary — volumes, energy, frequency — and within which limits.

milestones.name: Milestones
milestones.body: Review points, revision dates, notice periods.

1.name: Lot 1 · North – Hub – East – South loop
1.scope: The four links chained together, with the East warehouse window as a condition.

2.name: Lot 2 · South → Hub corridor
2.scope: The two subsidiaries’ flows to the hub, kept out of the loop.

partners: Regional road carrier able to chain several sites in the same rotation (lot 1).
Regional road carrier on the South → Hub corridor (lot 2).
loop.offerReading: Example of reading: an offer assuming three weekly rotations where the lot asks for five is not comparable with another — it is first brought to the same scope.

1.name: Lot 1 · Pooled South → Hub corridor
1.scope: Both subsidiaries’ flows grouped in a single lot, with an allocation key.

partners: Regional road carrier on the South → Hub corridor.
Groupage provider, if the shared volume does not fill a vehicle.
pooling.offerReading: Example of reading: one offer may price the shared lot only, another each subsidiary separately; they are compared once put on the same basis.

1.name: Lot 1 · North → Hub, three departures a week
1.scope: A reduced rhythm, with buffer-stock conditions on the receiving side.

partners: Regional road carrier on the North → Hub link.
frequency.offerReading: Example of reading: price per departure rises as rhythm drops; the comparison is on the full weekly cost, not the unit price.

1.name: Lot 1 · Hub → East warehouse by rail-road
1.scope: Pre-haulage, rail traction, post-haulage, handling at both terminals.

partners: Rail-road operator on the Hub → East warehouse corridor.
modal.offerReading: Example of reading: one offer may include terminal haulage, another not; they are only comparable once the scope is aligned.

1.name: Lot 1 · North → Hub → East in electric traction
1.scope: The two links with charging confirmed at both ends.

2.name: Lot 2 · Remaining links
2.scope: The other links, as they are, until charging infrastructure is in place.

partners: Carrier with electric vehicles suited to lot 1.
Regional road carrier for the remaining links (lot 2).
electric.offerReading: Example of reading: vehicle availability and charging power are conditions of the offer, not details.
